steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Procurement is the process of sourcing and purchasing materials: choosing reliable suppliers who offer the right quality, price, and delivery times.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Buffer stock is the minimum level of stock a business holds to prevent running out if demand unexpectedly increases or supply is delayed - a safety net.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Just-in-time (JIT) stock control means ordering stock to arrive only when needed: eliminates storage costs but requires reliable suppliers and accurate demand forecasting.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The bar gate stock control chart shows: maximum stock level, buffer stock level, re-order level (when to order), and lead time (time between ordering and delivery).

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: When discussing stock management, always consider the TYPE of product: perishable vs non-perishable changes the calculation. Link stock management to cash flow: excess stock ties up cash that could be used elsewhere. JIT questions need a balanced answer: cost savings vs risk of stockouts.
